messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: prefix-cache-miss surge detected across us-west-2. Auto-alert triggered at 2026-03-15T02:13:54Z. Escalation to eng-sre oncall. Link: https://ops.redwood/example/incident/2167891234
oncall-bot: Incident severity: P1. Symptoms: 5xx upstream errors + token latency spike + customer errors for real-time generation routes. Affected service: kv-prefix-cache (read path).
elaine: I'm on it. pulling up dashboards now. tagging @raj for cache runtime and @matt for customer impact.
elaine: Quick ask — any ongoing deploys in us-west-2 in the last 30m?
raj: saw a small canary for model-routing rolled ~00:59Z, not sure it's related. No explicit cache key changes in that PR but there was a library bump (kv-client v2.4.1). Investigating.
matt: Support: customer-facing errors started ~02:05Z, spike in 5xx for realtime-gen routes. A few paying customers reported request timeouts and degraded streaming. Logged escalations: CS-4552, CS-4553.
kevin: Pulling KV hit/miss time-series now. Early numbers: prefix-hit-rate dropped from ~92% to ~12% within 4m window. That's huge.
ops-bot: Collected logs: https://logs.redwood/streams/2167891234 (retention note: short). Run `rb query` to fetch slices.
elaine: Ok timeline draft (wip):
- 01:59:12Z deployment: model-routing canary (observed)
- 02:05:08Z first customer error reported (CS-4552)
- 02:08:10Z alert threshold crossed (prefix-hit-rate < 20%)
- 02:11:44Z oncall-bot escalated to P1
- 02:14:00Z mitigation: disable kv-client v2.4.1 canary on 3 nodes (in progress)
Please confirm or add.
raj: Adding: 01:58:55Z - kv-client v2.4.1 rollout started on 6 instances (staggered).
raj: Hypothesis A [under investigation]: kv-client v2.4.1 introduced a subtle hash change resulting in cache key prefix mismatch -> mass cache invalidation on reads.
raj: Hypothesis B [under investigation]: upstream index shard lag led to cache TTL misalign and eviction storm.
elaine: Can someone grab a sample of kv-client logs around 02:05 with the prefix hashing debug flag? Use: `kubectl logs -l app=kv-client -n prod --since=15m | grep prefix:`
kevin: Pasted sample below (masking IDs):
```
[02:04:58Z] kv-client.INFO prefix_calc old: "pref:abc123" new: "pref:abC123"
[02:04:59Z] kv-client.WARN cache_miss key=pref:abC123 ttl=0
[02:05:03Z] kv-client.ERROR cache_miss_rate=0.88 host=kv-03
```
lisa: That `old` vs `new` prefix casing looks suspicious — could be a normalization fix in v2.4.1.
matt: Customer impact summary for timeline: ~270 requests failed with 5xx in window, 4 customers experienced >20% error rates, one customer had production traffic routed to fallback model for ~9m. Tracked customers: Osprey, Rivulet, Notebookly.
elaine: Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Roll back kv-client to v2.4.0 across affected nodes (fastest).
2) Add a runtime key-normalization shim in front of cache reads (medium).
3) Increase cache TTLs and pre-warm prefixes (slow; later).
Which can oncall do immediately?
raj: I can roll back canary on the 6 instances now. I'll start with the oldest nodes and monitor prefix-hit-rate.
elaine: Do it. Post `kubectl rollout undo` command when you start. Tag me.
raj: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo daemonset/kv-client --to-revision=2026031400` starting now on nodes kv-01..kv-06.
ops-bot: Rollback started: kv-client -> v2.4.0 on 6 nodes. Progress: 2/6 succeeded.
kevin: Metrics update: prefix-hit-rate climbed from 12% -> 46% after 2 nodes rolled back (02:21Z). Latency decreasing.
lisa: I'm running a targeted prefix pre-warm for top-100 prefixes for the affected customers (small extra load). Using: `rb task prewarm --prefix-file=top100.txt --region=us-west-2`.
matt: CS notified customers Osprey and Notebookly; monitoring their dashboards. They've acknowledged and are standing by.
elaine: Hypothesis A status: [likely] based on log samples and quick recovery after rollback in-progress. Keep Hypothesis B open until we verify shard health.
raj: Collecting a focused trace for one failing request. Dumped KV key traces: https://traces.redwood/trace/abc-2167891234 (includes stack and key normalization path).
kevin: Added raw hit/miss timeline snapshot: https://metrics.redwood/dash/snap/2167891234-hitmiss.png
elaine: Next actions:
- raj: finish rollback and confirm all nodes v2.4.0 (ETA 8m)
- kevin: correlate shard lag metrics and eviction rate (ETA 10m)
- lisa: continue prefix pre-warm for customers (ETA 5m)
- matt: consolidate customer impact notes for RC (ETA 10m)
- elaine: I'll keep this thread as RCA coordination.
ops-bot: Note: Saved log bundle to /archives/2167891234/logbundle.tar.gz (TTL 7d).
raj: rollback complete on 6/6 nodes at 02:28:12Z. Observed prefix-hit-rate now ~89%.
kevin: eviction rate normalized. No persistent shard lag. Evidence points away from Hypothesis B.
elaine: Confirming status: service returning to normal, customer errors dropping to baseline. Tentatively root cause: kv-client v2.4.1 introduced normalization change that altered prefix case -> resulted in effective prefix mismatch & large cache miss wave.
elaine: Marking Hypothesis A as [confirmed].
elaine: Follow-ups for postmortem:
- PR review of kv-client v2.4.1 for normalization behavior (owner: raj)
- Add unit tests for prefix normalization and cross-version compatibility (owner: raj)
- Add a canary test for cache hit-rate on client upgrades (owner: eng-sre)
- Customer communication draft for impacted customers (owner: matt)
- Archive logs and metrics to S3 with full retention, attach to postmortem (owner: ops-bot)
matt: I'll draft customer comms and loop in legal if needed.
elaine: Thanks team. I'll start postmortem skeleton and set a follow-up meeting 1h. Closing live mitigation. If anything spikes, re-open thread. :thumbsup:
